item.title: Over-the-Toilet Storage: Measure Clearance Before Choosing Shelves
item.description: The wall above a toilet can hold useful storage in a small bathroom, but it is also an easy place to install the wrong shelf. A unit can fit the wall and still block the tank lid, crowd the person sitting below it or make a service panel hard to reach. Measure the toilet and the storage together. The goal is not to fill every inch above the tank, but to add a small amount of reachable storage without interfering with normal use or maintenance.

item.title: Towel Storage for a Small Bathroom With No Wall Space
item.description: When a small bathroom has no free wall for a towel bar, the answer is usually not a bigger rack. It is a clearer split of jobs: a damp towel needs air and a place to hang open, while clean spares need a dry place to wait. Once those two needs have separate homes, the room gets easier to use. This guide starts with a towel count, then measures the door, the floor and the cabinet fronts before comparing options.

item.title: Where to Store Cleaning Supplies With No Bathroom Closet
item.description: A bathroom with no storage closet still has to hold the products that do the dirtiest work: toilet bowl cleaner, an all-purpose spray, a scrub brush and a stack of cloths. In a small apartment they usually end up under the sink, on the tank or on the floor beside the toilet, which are the easiest places for a child or a pet to reach. This guide builds a compact, safe setup around the layout in the cover photo: one locked wall cabinet and one slim rolling cart.
